$comment: Target profile for yarrow. A sun-loving generalist of open ground, so it uses the spectral (meadow) model like arnica, with a much wider elevation band and no subalpine bias. Bands are set from where research-grade Kootenay records sit on the DEM (see docs/species-selection.md) widened by the published range.
habitat_note: Open, sunny ground from valley grassland and roadsides to subalpine and alpine meadows: dry to moist, often on thin or disturbed soils. Common in open forest gaps but not under closed canopy. Native A. millefolium (vars. borealis / occidentalis) is the plant here; it is a common colonist of roadsides and cutblocks, so logged ground is not penalised.

terrain_subweights.$comment: Elevation is nearly uninformative for a plant found from 450 m to the alpine, so most of the terrain weight is on slope and a gentle sunny-aspect preference.

observations.$comment: 79 research-grade records in the AOI, 402 across the Kootenays - enough for the boost to carry real signal. iNaturalist treats A. millefolium as a complex, and records filed under a variety match the target by name prefix. Sneezewort (A. ptarmica) is a rare garden escape of wet ground and is down-weighted.

elevation_m.$comment: Records run 475-2135 m (p05-p95). The lower bound sits below the valley floor so only the upper side bites.

aspect.$comment: A broad sun preference (SSW, +-80 deg full credit), not a filter: yarrow grows on every aspect in the open, but most abundantly on warm, dry ones.

vegetation.$comment: NDMI closure calibration is a property of the sensor and the region, not the species, so the ndmi and texture blocks are arnica's unchanged.

ndvi.$comment: Lower floor than arnica: yarrow is common on dry grassland and gravelly roadsides that never green up past 0.35.

logging.$comment: Neutral (1.0): yarrow is a regular early colonist of cutblocks and landings, so unlike arnica a regenerating block is real habitat, not a false positive.

validation.$comment: Heart-leaved arnica is a forest-understory plant recorded by the same people on the same trails. Beating it means the model tracks openness, not access.
